chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Thal'abah ibn Maymun, from Abdul Malik ibn Utba, who said:

I said, 'I do not cease to give the man money, and he says, 'It has perished or gone.' So what is a strategy with you to sort it out for me?' He said, 'Give the man one thousand dirhams and lend it to him, and give him twenty dirhams to work with all of the money, and you should say, 'This is the capital of my wealth, and this is the capital of your wealth, so whatever you attain from these two together, it is between me and you.' So I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about that, and he said, 'There is no problem with it.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no problem with it

ai.seo_question: How to protect a loan from loss in Islamic commercial jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated by Imam al-Sadiq (AS), validates a specific commercial stratagem (hi'lah) where a lender splits funds into a loan and an investment partnership to mitigate the risk of total loss if the debtor claims insolvency. By treating the small portion as working capital with shared profit/loss, the lender secures a claim on the debtor's earnings, reflecting the Shia juristic principle of utilizing flexible contractual forms to protect rights in trade. This mechanism highlights the practical application of fiqh in mitigating financial uncertainty while maintaining the validity of both loan and partnership elements.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Sa’alba Bin Maymoun, from Abdul Malik Bin Utba who said,

‘I said, ‘I do not cease to give the goods to the man, and he is saying, ‘It has perished, or gone’. So what is a strategy with you to sort it out for me?’ So he (the planner) said, ‘Give the man one thousand Dirhams and lend it to him, and give him twenty Dirhams to work with all of the goods, and you should be saying, ‘This is the capital of my wealth, and this is the capital of your wealth, so whatever you attain from these two together, so it would be between me and you’. So I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about that, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with it’.
en.sarwar: 16. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from Tha’labah ibn Maymun from ‘Abd al- Malik ibn ‘Utbah who has said the following: “‘I still give goods to this man and he says that it is destroyed or is spent, so what kind of plan can help it?’

He (the planner) said, ‘You can give the man one thousand dirham and give it to him as loan; then give him twenty dirham to work with the asset and say to him, “This is my capital and that is your capital. Whatever you gain thereof is between both of us.’” I asked about it from ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, who said, ‘It is not unlawful.’”
